sections.title: Build and package the API image
sections.what: Builds the API in stages and produces a container image that starts the compiled API on port 3000 as a restricted user.
sections.why: The header states that the build is multi-stage to keep the image small.
sections.watch_out: Real secrets must be provided when the container runs. The placeholder database address is only for the build step.

summary: A recipe that packages the API into a compact container image for deployment.
purpose: Produces a production image that runs the compiled API as a non-administrator user on port 3000.
why: The header says the build is multi-stage to keep the final image small, which is the stated goal of the design.
how: 1) Starts from a small Node.js base image and installs pnpm. 2) Installs the dependencies from the lock file. 3) Generates the database client code and builds the API. 4) Starts a fresh image, copies only the built output and needed modules, creates a restricted user, and sets the start command to run the built entry point.
inputs: The source code, the lock file and package manifests, and an optional database address build argument that defaults to a placeholder.
outputs: A container image that runs the API.
risks: The database address is a placeholder used only while building. Real secrets must be supplied when the container runs, not baked in at build time. Values passed as build arguments can be seen in the image history. The final image copies all node modules, so it is not as small as it could be.
debug: If the build fails at the database generation step, check that the database package is included and that the placeholder address is valid. If the container starts and then exits, check the runtime environment variables and confirm that the built entry point exists after the build step.
